What we can be sure of is that Apple will be raising prices when the iPhone 18 Pro launches next month. The company earlier raised prices across the board to reflect rising memory costs, but at that time did not adjust existing iPhone pricing—however, that situation was always only temporary.

Still, two sources indicate that the starting price of this year's Pro model will be USD 1,399—but I really find it hard to believe Apple would go that far...

Don't get me wrong: Apple has made it very clear to the outside world that they are genuinely committed to protecting profit margins and are not afraid of significant price hikes. For example, the base-model MacBook Air went from USD 1,099 to USD 1,299, an increase of USD 200. Even the MacBook Neo—which initially pleasantly surprised everyone with its USD 599 starting price—has also gone up by USD 100.

But a USD 300 increase to the iPhone Pro starting price is a different matter. Apple has only ever applied such steep hikes to even more expensive products in the past.

The biggest increase in the lineup, at USD 300, is the base-model MacBook Pro, which went from USD 1,699 to USD 1,999. That's undoubtedly a sizable jump, close to 18%. But if the iPhone 18 Pro goes up by USD 300 over its predecessor, that would work out to a staggering 27% increase.

Again, this kind of increase isn't entirely impossible. Some MacBook configuration upgrades, for instance, have nearly doubled in price, and Apple has always been keen to protect its margins. Still, Tim Cook has hinted on earnings calls that the company is not absolutely insistent on defending margins at all costs.

On the sales side, I do think this price hike will put a lot of people off upgrading, especially given that next year's Pro model looks like the real showstopper.

On the other hand, the Apple Upgrade program can take some of the sting out of the price increase. Consumers may feel that leasing an iPhone 18 Pro for a year and then upgrading to the 20th anniversary edition next year is a pretty good deal. But for those paying outright, an increase of this size will certainly give them pause.

What do you think? Do you consider a USD 300 increase reasonable? Or do you feel even Apple might not dare attempt a 27% hike? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
